title: Borrowing steps in the clock computation
statement: Let $K$ and $W$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $c$ be a configuration of $W$ on $x$, let $q$ be a state of $W$, let $r$ be an output register, let $i,j\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{rest}$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $kt$ and $kh$ specify the contents and head positions of the work tapes of $K$. Start the clock machine for $K$ and $W$ with simulated configuration $c$, simulated state $q$, register $r$, counter-tape contents storing $i$ true symbols followed by $j$ false symbols and then $\mathrm{rest}$, counter head at position $i$, the specified tapes of $K$, and empty output. After $j$ steps, its state is still the decrement state for $q,r$, its simulated configuration and $K$ tapes are unchanged, and the counter tape stores $i+j$ true symbols followed by $\mathrm{rest}$ with its head at position $i+j$; its output remains empty.
hypotheses_covered: Specified contents $kt$ and head positions $kh$ for $K$'s work tapes
